variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
name="Zsh User"
local age=30
readonly OS="Linux"
variables.notes: Similar to bash, but supports local scoping natively in functions.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Zsh mostly uses strings, but supports integer arrays and associative arrays.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if [[ $a -gt $b ]]; then
  echo "Greater"
elif [[ $a -eq $b ]]; then
  echo "Equal"
else
  echo "Less"
fi

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
for i in {1..5}; do
  echo $i
done

maps.title: Maps

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
command || echo "Failed"
# or
set -e # exit on error

comments.title: Comments & Script Headers
comments.notes: Zsh uses # for comments with script headers.

numbers.title: Numbers & Arithmetic
numbers.notes: Zsh supports shell integer arithmetic and numeric expressions.

booleans.title: Booleans & Exit Codes
booleans.notes: Zsh evaluates boolean status through exit codes (0 = success) and boolean primitives.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Coercion
type_casting.code:
str_val="42"
# Arithmetic context forces integer coercion
num=$((str_val + 0))
type_casting.notes: Zsh handles type conversion explicitly via type accelerators [type] or arithmetic evaluation.

strings.title: Strings & Quoting
strings.code:
single='Literal single quotes'
double="Expanded: ${USER}"
multiline="Line 1
Line 2"
strings.notes: Zsh differentiates between single quotes (literal) and double quotes (variable expansion).

string_formatting.title: String Interpolation
string_formatting.notes: Zsh provides in-string variable interpolation and printf formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Case
pattern_matching.notes: Zsh matches patterns with case statements or switch blocks with glob matching.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.code:
# Brace expansion
for i in {1..10..2}; do
    echo "$i"
done
range.notes: Zsh constructs ranges with brace expansion {start..end} or range operators ..

iterators.title: Pipes & Iterators
iterators.code:
while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "$line"
done < "file.txt"
iterators.notes: Zsh streams data elements through command pipelines and loop iteration.

oop_classes.title: Classes / Structured Functions
oop_classes.notes: Zsh defines reusable components through classes (PowerShell 5+) or modular functions.

lists.title: Arrays & Collections
lists.code:
items=("apple" "banana" "cherry")
items+=("date")
echo "${items[0]}" # apple
echo "${items[@]}" # all elements
lists.notes: Zsh manages arrays using array lists @() or whitespace-delimited shell arrays.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Zsh emulates tuples through string delimiters, .NET Tuples, or positional variables.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Lists
sets.notes: Zsh models unique sets using associative arrays or underlying runtime sets.

modules_import.title: Sourcing & Modules
modules_import.code:
# Source an external script
source ./utils.sh
# or: . ./utils.sh
modules_import.notes: Zsh imports external functions using source (. in POSIX) or Import-Module.
